**RQ10:** Visualization of the learning process for a BM agent across some representative episodes.
  
For more details, check the research questions document.

```{r}
#| label: setup

# To make sure r virtual environment is loaded when executing this script from python
library(renv)
renv::load()
library(tidyverse)
library(arrow)
library(ggh4x)
library(patchwork)
library(xml2)
library(glue)
library(gt)
library(jsonlite)
library(ggtext)
```

```{r}
#| label: load_custom_functions

library(here)

# Load custom theme
source(file = here("r","shared","theme.R"))

# Make it global theme (every plot automatically uses it)
theme_set(theme_thesis())
```

```{r}
#| label: data

# This function helps us to create reliable file paths
data_dir <- here("r","RQ10","data")

# Dynamic data import
# 1) list.files(): returns a vector with the file paths
# 2) set_names(): transforms it into a named vector, with names equal to the filename without extension. This functions are vectorized, thats why it works
# 3) map(): maps the function to every parquet file. It returns a list, where each element is a df
data <- list.files(data_dir, pattern="\\.parquet$", full.names = TRUE) |> 
  (\(x) set_names(x, tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(x))))() |> 
  map(read_parquet)
```

```{r}
#| label: get_warm_up_period(exploration)

# It's not perfectly precise — the true per-agent start is episode > 24 and all routes visited, so some agents start a few episodes later than 24. But it's the honest guaranteed floor ("no agent has started learning before this point"), it's already computed for every run via config.warm_up, and given the plot already treats each seed's trajectory independently without forcing alignment (per the existing code comment about seeds finishing at very different episode counts), a single shared floor line is consistent with that treatment rather than adding seed-specific precision the rest of the plot doesn't have either.

exploration_phase_floor <- as.numeric(unique(data$agents_od$warm_up))
```

```{r}
#| label: agent_od
agent_id <- data$agent_debug_trace$id |> unique()
agent_id_info <- data$agents_od |> 
  filter(
    id == agent_id
  ) |> 
  select(id, origin, destination, departure_time) |> 
  slice_head(n = 1) |> 
  mutate(
    id_fmt = str_replace(id,"agent_","")
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: network_edge_shapes

# Non-internal <edge> elements each have exactly one <lane> child with a
# "shape" attribute (a straight polyline "x1,y1 x2,y2 ..."), which is the
# edge's physical geometry — reused both to draw route trajectories and as
# the light-gray full-network backdrop that gives them spatial context.

# Read XML of the network used for this run
network_stem <- data$agents_od$network |> unique()
network_filename <- paste0(network_stem, ".xml")
all_networks <- list.files(
  here("sumo", "net"),
  pattern = "\\.net\\.xml$",
  recursive = TRUE,
  full.names = TRUE
)
network_matches <- all_networks[basename(all_networks) == network_filename]
if (length(network_matches) != 1) {
  stop(glue(
    "Expected exactly one network file named '{network_filename}' under sumo/net/, ",
    "found {length(network_matches)}."
  ))
}
network_path <- network_matches

# Function to parse the network XML edge shapes attributes.
# In particular:
# 1. SUMO shape attribute string has two points "x,y" separated by an space. 
# Example: 
# "107.20,-301.60 192.80,-301.60"
#    x1     y1      x2      y2
# 2. We wanna convert it to a df:
# | x      | y       |
# |--------|---------|
# | 107.20 | -301.60 |
# | 192.80 | -301.60 |

########
# Steps:
########
# 1. str_split(shape_str, " ")[[1]]: Splits on spaces. The [[1]] is because this function can accept more than one input string, and it returns a list with as much elements as input strings. So, with [[1]] we are saying that we want the results of separating by spaces the first (and only) string we passed as input.
# Result: c("107.20,-301.60", "192.80,-301.60")

# 2. str_split(","): Separate by comma
# Result: list(c("107.20", "-301.60"), c("192.80", "-301.60"))

# 3. map_chr(points,1): Walks the list and pulls out element 1 (x-string) from every point.
# Result: c("107.20", "192.80")
parse_shape <- function(shape_str) {
  points <- str_split(shape_str, " ")[[1]] |> str_split(",")
  tibble(
    x = as.numeric(map_chr(points, 1)),
    y = as.numeric(map_chr(points, 2))
  )
}

# Find all relevant edges elements of the network
network_edges <- xml_find_all(read_xml(network_path), "//edge[not(@function='internal')]")

# We create a tibble with two columns:
# 1. edge: (vectorized) For every edge it pulls out the id attribute giving one character vector — e.g. c("E10_11_EB", "E10_11_WB", ...)
# 2. shape_str: 
#   xml_find_first(): Find only first match. Basically for every edge, it pulls out the first lane child element. Because input were n edges, output is n lane elements as well.
# Then it pulls out the shape of the lane.
# So we end up with a tibble that contains the edges and its shapes,
# and its well aligned (since both columns are build from the same set of edges "network_edges" on the same order, is guarantee they are correctly aligned)
# Example:
# ┌───────────┬─────────────────────────────────┐
# │   edge    │            shape_str            │
# ├───────────┼─────────────────────────────────┤
# │ E10_11_EB │ "107.20,-301.60 192.80,-301.60" │
# └───────────┴─────────────────────────────────┘

# |> mutate(): Parses the shape of the edge as we saw before. Each cell is an entire small tibble containing the two points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) for that edge
# Example:
# ┌───────────┬───────────────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
# │   edge    │           shape_str           │                     shape                      │
# ├───────────┼───────────────────────────────┼────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
# │ E10_11_EB │ "107.20,-301.60               │ tibble(x=c(107.20,192.80),                     │
# │           │ 192.80,-301.60"               │ y=c(-301.60,-301.60))                          │
# └───────────┴───────────────────────────────┴────────────────────────────────────────────────┘


edge_shapes <- tibble(
  edge = xml_attr(network_edges, "id"),
  shape_str = xml_attr(xml_find_first(network_edges, "./lane[1]"), "shape")
) |>
  mutate(shape = map(shape_str, parse_shape)) |>
  select(-shape_str)

# We convert to long format
# Example one edge-row with a 2-point shape becomes 2 rows
# ┌───────────┬────────┬─────────┐
# │   edge    │   x    │    y    │
# ├───────────┼────────┼─────────┤
# │ E10_11_EB │ 107.20 │ -301.60 │
# ├───────────┼────────┼─────────┤
# │ E10_11_EB │ 192.80 │ -301.60 │
# └───────────┴────────┴─────────┘
network_backdrop <- edge_shapes |>
  unnest(shape)
```


```{r}
#| label: agent_routes
routes_agent <- data$od_routes_bm |> 
  mutate(
    memory_level = as.numeric(memory_level)
  ) |> 
  filter(
    origin == agent_id_info$origin,
    dest == agent_id_info$destination,
    memory_level == min(memory_level)
  ) |> 
  select(-c(warm_up, network, run_id, memory_level))
```

```{r}
#| label: paths_factor
path_levels <- routes_agent$route_id |> unique()
path_levels_labels <- map_chr(path_levels, \(x) paste0("P", x+1))
```

```{r}
#| label: route_geometry

# Builds one ordered polyline per route by walking od_routes' edges in
# step order and concatenating each edge's shape points
build_route_geometry <- function(od_routes_df) {
  od_routes_df |>
    filter(
      origin == agent_id_info$origin,
      dest == agent_id_info$destination
    ) |> 
    arrange(route_id, step) |>
    left_join(edge_shapes, by = "edge") |>
    unnest(shape) |>
    select(route_id, edge, x, y)
}

route_geometry <- build_route_geometry(
  data$od_routes_bm |> 
  mutate(
    memory_level = as.numeric(memory_level)
  ) |> 
  filter(
    memory_level == min(memory_level)
  ) |> 
  select(-c(run_id, memory_level, network, warm_up))
  ) |> 
  mutate(
    route_id = factor(route_id, levels = path_levels, labels = path_levels_labels)
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: od_markers

# Origin/destination labels are placed at the midpoint of the origin/dest
# edge's shape (mean of its shape points — exact midpoint for the typical
# 2-point straight edge) rather than at its start/end vertex, so the label
# sits centered along the edge instead of right on top of a corner. Not
# faceted by algorithm (same OD for both), so ggplot repeats it on both panels.
roles_levels <- c("Origin", "Destination")
roles_labels <- c("Origin edge", "Destination edge")

od_markers <- bind_rows(
  Origin = edge_shapes |>
    filter(edge == agent_id_info$origin) |>
    unnest(shape) |>
    summarise(x = mean(x), y = mean(y)),
  Destination = edge_shapes |>
    filter(edge == agent_id_info$destination) |>
    unnest(shape) |>
    summarise(x = mean(x), y = mean(y)),
  .id = "role"
) |>
  mutate(role = factor(role, levels = roles_levels, labels = roles_labels))
```

```{r}
#| label: route_segments

# geom_path can't show direction of travel, and without it a route that
# doubles back (e.g. starts on a westbound edge before turning towards a
# destination to the east) reads as an arbitrary detour. Turning each
# route into (x, y) -> (xend, yend) segments lets us attach an arrowhead
# to specific edges instead of the whole line.
route_segments <- route_geometry |>
  group_by(route_id, edge) |>
  mutate(xend = lead(x), yend = lead(y)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(xend))

# Only the origin/destination edges get an arrowhead — enough to show
# initial/final direction of travel (e.g. why a route detours west first)
# without cluttering every intermediate edge along the route. Each row's
# `edge` is the edge its *start* point belongs to, so filtering on it picks
# out exactly that edge's own segment
route_endpoint_segments <- route_segments |>
  filter(edge %in% c(agent_id_info$origin)) |> 
  group_by(edge) |> 
  slice_head(n = 1) |> 
  select(-route_id)
```

```{r}
#| label: reshape_json

# Create vectors that will contain name of columns after widening 
# old: Refers to the automatic names tidyverse give them
# labels: Refers to the names I put instead
p_path_old_names <- map_chr(path_levels, \(x) paste0("p,", x+1))
p_path_labels <- map_chr(path_levels, \(x) paste0("p_P", x+1))
PT_path_old_names <- map_chr(path_levels, \(x) paste0("perceived_travel_times,", x+1))
PT_path_labels <- map_chr(path_levels, \(x) paste0("PT_P", x+1))

agent_debug_trace_df <- data$agent_debug_trace |>
  mutate(memory_level = as.numeric(memory_level)) |>
  select(-c(history,run_id,network, warm_up, id)) |>
  unnest_wider(
    p,
    names_sep = ",",
  ) |> 
  rename_with(~p_path_labels, p_path_old_names) |> 
  unnest_wider(
    perceived_travel_times,
    names_sep = ","
  ) |> 
  rename_with(~PT_path_labels, PT_path_old_names) |>
  mutate(chosen = paste0("P", chosen + 1)) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = matches("^(p|PT)_P\\d+$"),
    names_to = c(".value", "path"),
    names_pattern = "(p|PT)_(P\\d+)"
  ) |>
  rename(
    ET = expected_travel_time
  ) |>
  mutate(
    is_chosen = path == chosen
  ) |>
  select(-chosen) |>
  # `p` is logged right after that episode's BM update (snapshot() is called
  # post-update in run_training_BM.py), so it's already the probability that
  # will be used to pick episode+1's route — i.e. the *end-of-episode* value.
  # The start-of-episode value used to make that episode's choice is simply
  # the previous episode's end value; episode 1 starts from BMAgent's initial
  # uniform prior (1 / n_routes), since no update has happened yet.
  arrange(memory_level, path, episode) |>
  group_by(memory_level, path) |>
  mutate(p_start = lag(p, default = 1 / length(path_levels_labels))) |>
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
#| label: main_plot

# Builds the faceted "agent learning across representative episodes" figure

plot_agent_learning <- function(memory_level_arg, representative_episodes) {
  
  #####################
  # 1. Annotations plot
  #####################
  
  # Drops the leading "0" off a 2-decimal probability (0.33 -> .33), and
  # collapses the two whole-number cases (0.00 -> 0, 1.00 -> 1) instead of
  # leaving a bare ".00" — handled before the generic strip so it doesn't
  # get double-stripped into "".
  fmt_p <- function(x) {
    s <- sprintf("%.2f", x)
    case_when(
      s == "0.00" ~ "0",
      s == "1.00" ~ "1",
      .default = sub("^0", "", s)
    )
  }

  # Per (episode, route) state for just the representative episodes: the
  # deviation driving the stimulus (ET - PT), forced to NA pre-warm-up since
  # ET/PT are both placeholder zeros. PT itself is only meaningful once
  # learning has started, so pre-warm-up rows show "PT=-" instead of "PT=0s".
  episode_state <- agent_debug_trace_df |>
    filter(
      memory_level == memory_level_arg,
      episode %in% representative_episodes
    ) |>
    mutate(
      is_warmup = episode <= exploration_phase_floor,
      # Pre-header — chosen_tt is the real SUMO travel time the agent
      # actually received that episode (the RL "reward"), unlike ET/PT/
      # stimulus it's a genuine value every episode, warm-up included.

      # Header
      ET_label = if_else(is_warmup, "ET=—", glue("ET={round(ET, 1)}s")),
      stimulus_label = if_else(is_warmup, "Stim=—", glue("Stim={round(stimulus, 2)}")),
      header = glue("{ET_label} {stimulus_label}"),
      # Route block
      route_id = factor(path, levels = path_levels_labels),
      PT_label = if_else(is_warmup, "—", glue("{round(PT)}s")),
      route_line = glue("{route_id} {fmt_p(p_start)}→{fmt_p(p)} {PT_label}"),
      # Bolded via markdown (rendered by ggtext::geom_richtext below) instead
      # of a trailing "*" — the chosen route should read as visually distinct
      # at a glance, not just flagged with a small extra character.
      route_line = if_else(is_chosen, glue("**{route_line}**"), route_line)
    )

  # One compact monospace label per representative episode, anchored at the
  # bottom-left corner of each facet panel. "Episode N" isn't repeated here
  # since facet_wrap's strip title already shows it.
  episode_annotations <- episode_state |>
    arrange(episode, route_id) |>
    group_by(episode) |>
    summarise(
      header = unique(header),
      chosen_route = route_id[is_chosen],
      chosen_tt = unique(chosen_tt),
      routes_block = paste(route_line, collapse = "<br>"),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) |>
    mutate(
      pre_header = glue("**Chosen: {chosen_route}** TT={chosen_tt}s"),
      # geom_richtext renders markdown, where a bare "\n" is a soft break
      # (collapsed to a space) — "<br>" is needed for an actual line break.
      label = paste(pre_header, header, routes_block, sep = "<br>"),
      x = min(network_backdrop$x) + 0.02 * diff(range(network_backdrop$x)),
      y = min(network_backdrop$y) + 0.03 * diff(range(network_backdrop$y))
    )

  #####################
  # 2. Network plot
  #####################
  
  # One copy of each route's polyline per representative episode, carrying
  # that episode's deviation/is_chosen so geom_path can facet by episode.
  # NOTE: deliberately not tidyr::crossing() — crossing() de-duplicates AND
  # SORTS its inputs, which silently scrambles route_geometry's edge-
  # traversal order (sorted by route_id/x/y instead) and makes geom_path
  # draw nonsense diagonals between physically unrelated points. map() +
  # list_rbind() just repeats route_geometry as-is, once per episode,
  # preserving its original row order.
  
  route_geometry_by_episode <- representative_episodes |>
    # map() produces a list of data frames:
    # episode 1 → route geometry
    # episode 25 → route geometry
    # episode 26 → route geometry
    map(\(ep) mutate(route_geometry, episode = ep)) |>
    # list_rbind() stacks all those data frames on top of each other
    list_rbind() |>
    left_join(
      episode_state |> select(episode, route_id, is_chosen),
      by = c("episode", "route_id")
    ) |> 
    filter(is_chosen)
  
  main_plot <- ggplot() +
    geom_path(
      data = network_backdrop,
      mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, group = edge),
      color = "grey80",
      linewidth = 0.3
    ) +
    geom_path(
      data = route_geometry_by_episode,
      mapping = aes(
        x = x, y = y,
        group = route_id,
      ),
      lineend = "round"
    ) +
    geom_segment(
      data = route_endpoint_segments,
      mapping = aes(
        x = x, y = y, xend = xend, yend = yend,
      ),
      lineend = "round",
      arrow = arrow(length = unit(0.20, "cm"), type = "closed")
    ) +
    ggrepel::geom_label_repel(
      data = od_markers,
      mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, label = role),

      # label appearance
      size = 2.5,
      fontface = "bold",
      label.size = NA,
      fill = alpha("white", 0.8),

      # repel behavior
      box.padding = 0.5,
      nudge_x = -1,

        # connector
      min.segment.length = 0,
      segment.size = 0.3,
      segment.color = "grey20",

      # reproducibility
      seed = 1,
    ) +
    ggtext::geom_richtext(
      data = episode_annotations,
      mapping = aes(x = x, y = y, label = label),
      hjust = 0,
      vjust = 0,
      size = 3.1,
      family = "mono",
      label.size = NA,
      fill = alpha("white", 0.85)
    ) +
    # Preserve network aspect ratio
    coord_equal() +
    theme(
      axis.text = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks = element_blank(),
      axis.title = element_blank(),
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      strip.text = element_text(
        size = 11,
        face = "bold"
      )
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~episode, ncol = 3, labeller = labeller(episode = \(x) paste("Episode", x)))
  
  # routes_guide_plot is static (candidate routes don't vary by
  # memory_level/episode — see plot_routes_guide chunk), so it's stacked
  # below the episode grid via patchwork rather than rebuilt per call: it
  # shows what P1/P2/P3 physically look like, since each episode panel above
  # only draws the one route actually chosen that episode.
  main_plot + plot_spacer() + routes_guide_small +
    plot_layout(widths = c(4.5, -0.8, 1)) +
    plot_annotation(
      title = "Evolution of Route Choice During Learning",
      subtitle = glue(
        "Agent {agent_id_info$id_fmt} | Departure time: {agent_id_info$departure_time}s | Memory level = {memory_level_arg}"
      )
    )
}
```

```{r}
#| label: plot_memory_1

# Chosen to trace the actual arc seen at memory_level = 1: uniform
# exploration, end of warm_up, early convergence toward one route, then a
# genuine regime switch to a different route mid-run, and final lock-in.
# Tune freely per memory_level — pass a different episode vector per call.
plot_agent_learning(memory_level_arg = 1, representative_episodes = c(1, 25, 26, 27, 34, 50))

ggsave(here("r","RQ10","figures","plot1_agent_learning_mem1.png"))
```
